newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybean rally lifts soyoil, soymeal.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybean rally lifts soyoil, soymeal.

text.p: A supply-related rally in CBOT soybean futures caused soymeal and soyoil futures to end higher Friday, floor traders and analysts said.
"July beans are holding everything up," said Sid Love, analyst with Kropf and Love Consulting.
July soybeans rallied the daily 30-cent-bushel trading limit on worries about available supplies of U.S. soybeans for spot shipment.
On Thursday, the U.S. Department of Agriculture issued forecasts that showed old crop ending stocks still hovered around 20-year lows.

Rail basis offers in cash soymeal markets were also seen as a source of strength for July soymeal. Basis climbed as much as $1.00 to $3.00 per ton higher because of tight soybean supplies, cash dealer said.
A strong weekly crush of 25.378 million bushels for the week ended June 11 was seen dampening buying enthusiasm in the soyoil pit, traders said.
CBOT July soymeal settled up $4.40 per ton at $281.10 and other months were $1.60 to $3.40 higher. July soyoil was up 0.09 cent a lb at 23.33 cents and other months were 0.05 to 0.12 cent higher.
In soymeal trade, Cargill and FIMAT Futures, Inc. each bought 400 lots July. Prudential Securities sold 200 lots July, pit sources said.
Commerical firms were buyers in the soyoil pit. ADM bought 300 lots July and 100 October, and Cargill bought 100 lots July.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 24,000 lots, compared with Thursday's actual volume of 22,612 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 10,000 lots, against Thursday's 8,770 lots.
